proposal: Give the golf fetcher a look-ahead so scheduled FUTURE PGA Tour / DP World Tour tournaments board from the static pipeline instead of being hand-boarded by research every week. Root cause: the shared validateESPNScoreboard drops any event with an empty competitors[] — correct for football/F1/tennis (a fixture needs two sides) but wrong for golf, where a tournament has no field until tournament week, so ESPN returns it as competitions:[{competitors:[]}]. Those future events were stripped BEFORE reaching golf.js's own 'scheduled tournament with no field yet' handling (golf.js lines 381–432), making that handler dead code for the look-ahead case. Fix is the smallest backward-compatible one: add a { requireCompetitors = true } option to validateESPNScoreboard (default unchanged → every other caller byte-identical) and have golf.js pass requireCompetitors:false in both its scoreboard-validation calls. This REACTIVATES existing code rather than adding machinery (the v2 bias), and deliberately does NOT alter the shared validator's default (self-repair's correct warning: that would wrongly affect all ESPN fetchers).
evidence: research-log 2026-10-12: the independent grader docked the run −10 for 'den gjentatte uløste strukturelle anbefalingen (golf-fetcher uten look-ahead = samme rotårsak som DP World/Baycurrent/Bermuda hver uke)'; the run's primary deliverable was hand-boarding the next PGA tournament (Butterfield Bermuda Championship) as source:ai-research because golf.json was empty forward.

self-repair-log 2026-10-12: diagnosed golf.js returns 0 tournaments — 'every upcoming event (Butterfield Bermuda, DP World India, Genesis) is dropped by the SHARED validateESPNScoreboard "missing_competitors" rule … future golf tournaments have no field/competitors until tournament week.' It correctly declined to touch the shared validator (would wrongly affect all ESPN fetchers), leaving a golf-scoped fix as the right path — exactly this change.

The self-repair diagnosis proves the future events FAIL specifically at the missing_competitors check, i.e. they PASS the earlier missing_competitions check — so they carry competitions:[{competitors:[]}] and relaxing only requireCompetitors (keeping the competitions-array requirement) is the precise, evidence-matched fix.

coverage-contracts.json: golf:pga-tour (min 1 upcoming within 21 d) breached week after week once the live tournament finished; golf is tier1 (wholesale) in catalog.json, so the next tournament is a coverage promise, not an owner follow. golf.json was served from retainLastGood (6 consecutive retains), frozen on the finished Baycurrent Classic with nothing forward.

golf.js already contained the full 'scheduled tournament with no field on ESPN yet' handling (lines 381–432: PGA-field verification → board with Norwegians, else fieldPending; DP World → fieldPending) — it was unreachable for future events because the shared validator stripped them upstream. The fix reactivates it; no new branch logic added.

npm test: 88 files / 1544 tests pass (+3 new in tests/response-validator.test.js pinning the default drops a competitor-less event, requireCompetitors:false keeps it, and a competition-less event is still dropped in both modes). node scripts/validate-events.js: 135 events, 0 errors.
expectedEffect: golf.json carries the next PGA Tour / DP World Tour tournament (as a fieldPending node until the field publishes) instead of going empty between events — free, hourly, from the static pipeline. The WP-243 golf:pga-tour contract stops breaching between tournaments; stale-retained/retainLastGood stops freezing golf.json forward. The research agent stops spending a pass hand-boarding a mechanically-available fixture every week, and the grader's recurring −10 for this structural flag clears.
howWeKnow: golf.json contains a future tournament (e.g. Butterfield Bermuda Championship) sourced from the fetcher, not hand-boarded as source:ai-research; coverage-contracts.json golf:pga-tour stays 'met' through the gap between tournaments; research-log's grader stops docking for the golf look-ahead structural recommendation.
notes: Smallest viable change (3 files, +49/−4): one optional validator param with an unchanged default + two golf call sites + a focused validator test. No per-tour segmentation or new fetcher machinery.

Default requireCompetitors:true preserves byte-identical behaviour for football/F1/tennis and every other validateESPNScoreboard caller — the response-validator and fetcher golden/unit tests all still pass unchanged.
Did NOT touch the shared validator's default (self-repair flagged altering it as a wrong fix affecting all ESPN fetchers) — the relaxation is opt-in and golf-only.
